name: Delivery Optimization: no peer-to-peer uploads
description: Downloads Windows and Store updates only from Microsoft, without serving them to other PCs.
mechanism: Sets the policy DODownloadMode=0 ('HTTP only, no peering') under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeliveryOptimization. Applied by the Delivery Optimization service to new download jobs.
benefit: No background upload traffic competing with games — relevant on slow upload links or routers prone to bufferbloat.
drawback: Households with several PCs lose LAN sharing of updates. Updates continue to download and install normally.
recommendedFor: Gaming PCs on connections with limited upload bandwidth.

name: Network adapter: don't allow Windows to turn it off
description: Clears 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power' on the active network adapter.
mechanism: Sets Enable=false on the adapter's root\wmi:MSPower_DeviceEnable instance — the same setting as Device Manager › adapter › Power Management.
benefit: Prevents the adapter from being powered down when idle, which can cause brief disconnects or latency spikes on wake.
drawback: Slightly higher idle power. Takes effect for future idle periods; on some drivers after reconnecting.
recommendedFor: PCs with connection drops after idle or on Wi-Fi.
evidence: Documented WMI class MSPower_DeviceEnable. Many modern adapters also have driver-level 'Green Ethernet'/'Energy Efficient Ethernet' options configured in the adapter's Advanced tab (not changed here).

name: MMCSS NetworkThrottlingIndex: disabled (expert)
description: Removes the multimedia network packet-processing limit.
mechanism: Sets NetworkThrottlingIndex=0xFFFFFFFF under ...\Multimedia\SystemProfile. While MMCSS-registered multimedia playback is active, Windows limits non-multimedia packet processing to this many packets per millisecond (default 10).
benefit: May help sustained high-bandwidth transfers while audio/video is playing.
drawback: Can increase CPU/DPC time under heavy network load and cause audio glitches. It does NOT reduce ping: it cannot change ISP routing, distance to the server, or Wi-Fi conditions.
recommendedFor: Only for users measuring a specific throughput problem during media playback.
evidence: Introduced with Windows Vista MMCSS (KB 948066). Independent testing shows no measurable latency benefit for online games on modern Windows. Not included in any profile.

name: TCP: acknowledge every segment on the active interface (expert)
description: Disables TCP delayed ACK for the active adapter's interface.
mechanism: Sets TcpAckFrequency=1 under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters\Interfaces\{active interface GUID}. Windows then ACKs each TCP segment instead of every second segment or after 200 ms.
benefit: Can reduce latency for TCP request/response traffic (some MMOs, game launchers, remote tools). Most fast-paced online games use UDP, where this has no effect.
drawback: More ACK packets and slightly more CPU/network overhead. Applies only to the adapter active when applied.
recommendedFor: Expert users testing a TCP-based game.
evidence: Microsoft KB 328890 documents TcpAckFrequency. TCPNoDelay is intentionally not offered: Winsock applications set TCP_NODELAY themselves and the registry value is not honoured for them.
